title: Incident communication field guide — draft
content:
Purpose
This field guide captures lightweight, engineer-focused communication recipes and a compact war-room checklist for incidents. Aim: allow a single on-call SRE to operate the initial comms loop (internal + external) with minimal overhead and consistent tone.

Quick TL;DR (for on-call)
- Post an initial internal one-liner in #ops-incident-bridge within 5 minutes.
- Create an incident ticket (ENG-YYYY) and put the ticket link in every update.
- Update public status page for customer-impacting incidents.
- Send customer-facing acknowledgement for affected customers within 30 minutes (if high-sev).
- Keep updates every 30–60 minutes until stability, then every 2–4 hours during recovery.

Tone & style guidance
- Internal: direct, technical, next-steps-oriented. Use concise bullets. Name the owner and ETA for next update.
- Public: plain language, avoid internal debugging detail, include what’s affected and a clear mitigation/ETA. Be empathetic and own the outcome.
- Customers with contracts: add SLA/upgrade notes only after coordinating with support/ops lead.

Roles and responsibilities
- Incident commander (IC): owns overall status and cadence; posts the public status update.
- Scribe: maintains the incident ticket notes and timeline.
- Communications lead (can be the IC): approves customer-facing language if the incident affects SLAs or >10% of requests.
- Engineering triage: runs mitigation steps and reports progress in the ticket.

When to update which channel
- #ops-incident-bridge (internal): initial notification, every update, escalation requests.
- Status page (public): Investigating -> Identified -> Service degraded/outage -> Mitigated -> Resolved.
- Dedicated customer email/CS ping: if customers are on an incident list or high-touch accounts affected.

Minimum internal war-room checklist (first 15 minutes)
- 0–3m: Confirm impact surface and severity (S1/S2/S3). Add short sentence: what failed, who noticed, rough scope.
- 3–7m: Spin up bridge and invite IC, Scribe, triage leads, and SRE on-call.
- 7–12m: Create incident ticket with tags (service, region, severity). Add initial logs/screenshots.
- 12–15m: Post initial internal notice and set cadence (e.g., 30m updates).
- 15m+: Post customer ack if customer-facing.

Annotated status page templates (keep short)
- Investigating (public)
  Title: "Degraded performance for Redwood API in us-west-2"
  Body: "We are aware of increased latency for the Redwood API in the us-west-2 region. Our engineers are investigating. Users may see slower responses or timeouts. Incident ID: {INCIDENT_ID}. Last updated: {TIMESTAMP}."

- Service Outage (public)
  Title: "API outage impacting text generation in us-west-2"
  Body: "We are experiencing a service outage affecting text generation requests in us-west-2. We are actively working on a fix and will provide updates every 30 minutes. Affected customers may see failed requests or errors. Incident ID: {INCIDENT_ID}."

- Resolved (public)
  Title: "Issue resolved — API performance restored"
  Body: "Service has been restored and normal traffic is returning. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support@redwood.ai and reference {INCIDENT_ID}. A post-incident summary will be published when available."

Customer-facing email templates
- Initial acknowledgement (concise)
  Subject: "Redwood status — {SHORT_DESCRIPTION} — {INCIDENT_ID}"
  Body: "Hi {CUSTOMER_NAME},

We’re investigating an issue affecting {AFFECTED_SERVICE}. Some requests may fail or be slower than usual. Our engineers are on it and we’ll follow up with an ETA in the next 30 minutes. Incident ID: {INCIDENT_ID}.

Thanks for your patience,
{IC_NAME} — Redwood Inference Operations"

- Update for major customers (after mitigation found)
  Subject: "Update: {SHORT_DESCRIPTION} — {INCIDENT_ID} — mitigation in progress"
  Body: "Hi {CUSTOMER_NAME},

An update on {INCIDENT_ID}: we’ve identified a resource contention issue on instances serving {MODEL/ENDPOINT}. We’ve applied a temporary routing change that has reduced errors for most customers. We expect full restoration within ~{ETA}. We will follow up when service is fully validated.

If you want direct help or to confirm traffic routing for your account, reply or ping your CSM.

{IC_NAME}
Redwood Inference"

- Post-resolve summary (to affected customers)
  Subject: "Incident report: {INCIDENT_ID} — {SHORT_DESCRIPTION}"
  Body: "Hi {CUSTOMER_NAME},

The incident affecting {AFFECTED_SERVICE} has been resolved at {RESOLUTION_TIME}. Root cause: {ROOT_CAUSE_SUMMARY}. Mitigation applied: {MITIGATION_SUMMARY}. Customer impact: {IMPACT_SUMMARY}. We estimate customers experienced {SCOPE_METRIC} of failed requests during the incident window. A full RCA will be published in Confluence.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Operations"

Internal short-form templates (for Slack)
- Initial post (use code block for key data)
  "INVESTIGATING: {SERVICE} — {ONE-LINER}
  Incident: {INCIDENT_ID} | Sev: {SEVERITY} | IC: {IC_NAME} | Ticket: {TICKET_LINK}"

- Update post
  "UPDATE {MINUTES}m: {SHORT_PROGRESS} | Next: {NEXT_STEP} | ETA: {ETA}"

- Call for help
  "ESCALATE: need DB team to check replica lag — contact @db-ops. Impact: 20% error rate on /v1/generate"

Rapid-check troubleshooting checklist (common causes)
- Autoscaler spinup/backoff: check pool utilization, instance health, and recent deploys.
- Downstream auth failures: check token errors and KMS errors in logs.
- Network/region routing: validate BGP/Cloud provider health pages and cross-region load balancer metrics.
- Cache/KV storms: watch hit rate and eviction metrics, inspect prefix distribution.
- Model runtime OOMs: review GPU OOM traces and tail latency spikes.

Escalation matrix (who to ping first)
- Networking/regional outage: @infra-networking, on-call infra lead
- Model serving errors: @serving-runtime, model infra on-call
- Billing/usage alpha anomalies: @platform-engineering
- Customer comms/legal: @customer-success, @legal on-call for PII concerns

Notes to self / open questions
- Should we make a small status-page snippet generator (CLI) that auto-populates {INCIDENT_ID}, region, and ETA from the incident ticket?
- Agree on customer cadence thresholds for S2 incidents (right now ambiguous).
- Add a short training doc for on-call engineers: examples of poor vs good public language.

Quick checklist for post-incident (first 24 hours)
- Stabilize and verify all services for 60 minutes.
- Draft a short public post-mortem outline and assign the author.
- Notify CS + account owners for any customers likely to be impacted.
- Add timeline and artifacts (screenshots, logs, traces) to incident ticket.

Appendix: sample small-incident one-liner library
- "Investigating increased 5xx rate for embeddings endpoint in eu-central-1"
- "Degraded chat latency after config rollout, rolling back now"
- "Temporary routing fallback applied for model x-small; monitoring"

End of draft — this doc is intentionally terse so it can be used as a quick reference in the middle of an incident. Feedback welcome — note items above to discuss on the next SRE sync.

Unresolved: preferred cadence for S2 customer emails, approval flow for legal review on customer impact language.
